rows.etymology: 43. Pr. kos ‘vagina’ and Kho. ċuk ‘vagina’. According to Turner, the Khowar word is the only modern derivation < *cukka- ‘anus, vulva’ (4860), but he adds a question mark (because of the dental affricate). The word is therefore better interpreted as metathe- sis < *kuċ or *kuč with reflexes besides just-mentioned Pr. in Kal. gušík ‘vulva’ and perhaps in Bur.ys. -khús ‘buttocks, anus’, P. kusso ‘a strumpet’ and khuccṇā ‘to have sexual intercourse with’, M. vāhtī kūs ‘the womb that bears’ (if not Pers. borrowing) and Munds Sant. kusbi ‘a strumpet’. This looks very close to PIE *kutsós ‘vulva’, but the survival of the affricate is perhaps suspicious (and Mallory and Adams derive modern Pers. kūn ‘ass’ from this lemma). Or is there connection with the Baltic- Iranian isogloss *kukîs ‘female pubic hair, vulva’ which has modern reflexes in nearby languages like Psht. kus (also P. and, as just pointed out, Bur.ys. khʊs ‘anus’) and Ind. kòs, and perhaps in Bur. gus ‘(married) woman; (with animals) female’ (but cf. also Bur. -ġúṣ ‘female genitals, vulva’ which is probably also contained in Kal. ǰabáṣ ‘prostitute or lady friend other than one’s wife’ with first syllable < OIA *yab- hyate ‘futuitur’ [10420] and second syllable cf. Bur. -ġúṣ and P. ghūssā ‘pudendum mulieris’). The words are certainly connected with Shgh. kawuč/ǰ ‘vagina’ and note also Greek κύσθoς ‘pudenda muliebra’ regarded by Beekes (PREG: 99) as originally pre-Greek. Čašule (2010: 46) derives from PIE *kutsós Bur.ys. -khús ‘anus’ and -khúśi dél- ‘sodomise’. In any case, here is yet another example for semantic-morphological amalgamations (see p. 224). Notes: (a) It is unclear whether Pr. kċʌ, kċə ‘podex, hip’ is etymologically related with Pr. kos. (b) Above *cukka- belongs to the same group as *cutta- ‘anus, vulva’ (4860) which seems to be the origin of Pr. sutˈog ‘penis’ and which Turner compares (ibid.) with Pers. cul ‘penis’. (c) For Par. būn ‘vulva’ Morgenstierne considers connection with Pers. baun, būn ‘uterus’. This is probably unrelated with K. pōna-bachĕ ‘(of a woman) one who has an ill-omened vulva’ and pōnuku ‘of, or belonging to, the anus or the vulva’ where pōna-bachĕ may be a synonym compound with first component < OIA (Mbh.) apāná- ‘the anus’, and regarding second component cf. Bshk. and Dara. boč ‘vulva’ (see above p. 353).
